title: IP Mascots
description: Six IP-mascot logo candidates from one identity brief — three directions, two takes each, generated with the logo & mascot playbook (references/logo-mascot.md; inspired by s1dashu/ip-as-logo-skill).

rows.label: Direction A — ember spirit — the spark of co-creation — one soft flame tuft

items.title: A1 — ember spirit, lower-right, charcoal ground
items.prompt:
Create one complete full-bleed 1:1 square image.
Background: fill the entire square with solid deep charcoal-black. Keep it visible in every open area and in the corners the mascot does not occupy.
Subject: place one highly simplified plump ember-spirit mascot — a rounded teardrop flame creature — on the background, reduced to one rounded continuous silhouette with one soft blunt flame tuft on top as its single defining feature.
Complexity: use 6-10 broad basic shapes, at most two broad internal color regions, and a face with two eyes and one mouth. Keep the symbol readable at 32 x 32.
Color behavior: use exactly three semantic colors in the complete artwork: vivid warm orange and soft warm cream as the two IP base colors, plus the charcoal background. The body is one broad orange mass; the two eyes and mouth are cream. Keep the mascot, its facial marks, and the background clearly separated. Tonal variation within either mascot color stays inside that color and is not an additional semantic color.
Composition: keep the mascot upright, emerging from the lower-right, filling about 85-95% of the square, with both paired identifying features visible.
Style: use an ultra-clean flat graphic treatment with minimal broad masses, thick rounded contours, and one clear shape in place of several explanatory details. Add an extremely, extremely subtle, almost imperceptible sense of depth through a barely-there neo-skeuomorphic treatment.
Finish: show only the mascot on the full-canvas background, with clean geometric surfaces and normal square outer corners.
Constraints: Use no text or watermark. Add no borders, frames, cards, or presentation masks. Include one mascot only, with no extra subjects or scenery. Keep the contours thick and rounded, without fragile lines or sharp tips. Add no photorealistic material, dramatic bevel, glossy hotspot, deep occlusion, extrusion, strong three-dimensional rendering, or external cast shadow. Keep the background solid and uniform, with no texture, vignette, or lighting variation.
